headline: Avoids the property development sector as too hard for compounding investors
reasoning: Property development by its nature requires constant recycling of capital: operators take risk to improve assets, then must sell or monetise and start again rather than compounding returns. This means investors face an ever-compounding element of risk rather than reward. The bigger the company gets the larger the bets required and the higher execution risk becomes. Stockland's 10-year results demonstrate this with every good year followed by excess risk in the next. Coleman also notes most Australians already have heavy property exposure through their own homes and investment properties, making additional listed property exposure redundant.
quote: the challenge in property development and property ownership from a compounding point of view if you want to think of investing as the goal of compounding growth year after year until hopefully an infinite time horizon though none of us will ever live that long is that in the property development game what they call a pipeline we as an investor have to call starting over because the nature of the business is to take something unloved put risk and capital into it to make it better and then having completed that exercise rather than sitting back and enjoying the fruits of your labor you have to either sell it or monetize it and then go again and so as an investor you are going to experience in the property sector in general in Stockland is no no unique beast in that a constantly compounding element of risk rather than reward because the bigger they get the bigger the gambles they have to take the higher the execution risk comes the more likelihood that you can't get one part of that pipeline right.
